findings.claim: DPDP commencement is phased. Machinery provisions started on publication; Consent Manager provisions follow after one year, and most core fiduciary duties and rights after eighteen months, in May 2027. As of 25 October 2026, those core duties have not all commenced. Printed 13 November dates and official 14 November publication descriptions differ.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: High for relative phases; Medium for the exact operative calendar day

findings.implication: Do not present the old repo’s May 13, 2027 as an independently settled day or use an agency forced-buy narrative. Track the statutory relative schedule and confirm the operative day before a legal deadline claim. Transitional timing is not a finding that current Indian privacy/IT obligations disappear.

findings.claim: On commencement, DPDP consent-based processing requires an informed, specific affirmative choice and purpose-limited necessary data. Withdrawal must be comparably easy. Identifiable student profiles and saved chats fall within the digital-personal-data design problem; a free launch does not establish an exemption.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: High for statute; product applicability requires implementation review

findings.claim: The enacted framework makes a fiduciary responsible for processors, requires a valid processor contract, provides correction/erasure rights, and requires security safeguards. The Rules specify security controls and breach notification. These substantive provisions share the deferred commencement schedule.

findings.claim: DPDP defines a child as under eighteen. Once the relevant provisions commence, child processing generally requires verifiable parental consent and restricts tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising, subject to prescribed exceptions. The Rules describe parental verification and narrow educational-institution exceptions.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: High for age and general rule; Medium for any specific exception claim

findings.claim: DPDP section 16 permits government restrictions on foreign transfers, and Rule 15 adds requirements that may be specified by government order for availability to foreign states or related entities. A destination-country recommendation does not reveal where the student’s data is processed.

findings.claim: EDPB guidance ties GDPR territorial scope to an EEA establishment, targeting people in the EEA with goods/services, or monitoring their behaviour there. Offering a free service can still qualify. A student’s interest in studying in Germany alone is not one of those tests.
findings.label: Data
findings.sourceDate: Current EDPB basics page accessed 2026-10-25; scope guidelines 2019/2020
findings.confidence: High for general territorial tests; applicability depends on real operations

findings.claim: The German Missions’ live study-visa checklist currently states EUR 11,904 livelihood funds and EUR 992 monthly blocked-account withdrawals, lists alternative financial evidence, and separately requests tuition-fee and insurance evidence. It distinguishes bachelor/preparatory and master documents, describes APS exceptions, and explicitly says complete documents do not guarantee a visa.

findings.implication: A budget alone, including the founder’s illustrative INR 10 lakh, cannot establish total affordability, admission or a visa. findings.claim: Hochschulkompass’s university-list downloads are free for personal use only; its page requires approval for all other uses, especially commercial use, including parts. Public visibility and zero price do not establish a reusable production-data licence.

findings.implication: Before adopting the old proposed institution spine, obtain permission or use data sources with explicit suitable rights and university-authoritative records. Keep source permissions alongside provenance. A free startup beta is not necessarily personal use; this finding does not settle every website/database/copyright issue.

gaps: Exact operative calendar day for the May 2027 core DPDP commencement requires resolution of printed-notification versus official publication descriptions; use the statutory eighteen-month schedule pending advice.
Current IT Act/SPDI and other pre-DPDP duties were not exhaustively mapped; do not infer a legal vacuum before core DPDP commencement.
No processor/model stack, company structure, actual retention practices, age mix or EU targeting has been chosen, so an as-built legal applicability/transfer assessment cannot yet be completed.
No current government transfer-restriction orders or production data licences were exhaustively cleared; perform a launch-specific check.

No source-backed rupee compliance cost, DPO staffing requirement for this startup, mandated certification, or general study-adviser licence finding was established. Obtain a scoped professional review rather than fabricate estimates.
No eligibility/visa prediction accuracy can be established from a government checklist; product-specific source coverage and quality evaluation remain necessary.
redFlags: Family/financial context and chat may contain unnecessary identifiable data; optional UI alone does not establish informed consent or lawful processing.
Under-18 students can enter the bachelor audience; an adult-professional-only premise from the old agency brief is no longer valid.
The proposed HRK download-based institution spine is not production-cleared by being free or publicly accessible.
No admission, visa or affordability guarantee can be supported by a generic profile or the INR 10 lakh illustration.
yellowFlags: DPDP dates in government summaries and printed Gazette differ by one day; avoid repeating a single hard deadline without qualification.
Foreign model/hosting processing cannot be assumed to remain inside India.
GDPR depends on real establishment/targeting/monitoring, not on destination alone.
Visa and university rules need separately versioned, current official evidence; source permissions and legal analysis are still required for real deployment.
summary: The free, student-facing pivot materially changes data and age assumptions. Design privacy and source rights before production; plan against the phased DPDP rules without turning them into a sales deadline. German official checklists give verifiable constraints, not a prediction of personal outcomes.
